input.quote: Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation, and the media on which the Software is distributed will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use, for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period").
input.rationale: There is an express conformance-to-Documentation warranty with repair/replace and, failing that, termination plus refund of prepaid fees, and a no-malicious-code warranty, so the remedy structure meets the playbook. The duration fails the fallback: the warranty runs only sixty (60) days from the Effective Date and in no event past December 31, 1999, whereas Acceptance Testing under Section 3.1 itself runs to December 31, 1999 — so the warranty would expire at or before acceptance, well short of even the 90-day software fallback. The redline sets a twelve (12) month period measured from acceptance and removes the calendar cut-off, and adds a professional and workmanlike warranty for Commerce One's installation, implementation and other professional services (currently absent). We note separately that the disclaimer text (p0084) appears truncated in this copy; on its face it disclaims only implied warranties and does not swallow the express warranties.

proposal.summary: Extend software/service warranty to 12 months from acceptance (removing the December 31, 1999 cut-off) and add a professional and workmanlike services warranty.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 60-day warranty running from the Effective Date and expiring no later than December 31, 1999 would lapse at or before acceptance under Section 3.1, so we have extended it to twelve (12) months from acceptance and added a professional and workmanlike standard for Commerce One's services, consistent with our playbook position. We can accept ninety (90) days from acceptance as a fallback if the longer period is an issue.

ops.oldText: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")
ops.newText: for a period of twelve (12) months from Corio's acceptance of the Software pursuant to Section 3.1 (the "Warranty Period")

ops.text: Commerce One further warrants that all installation, implementation, training and other professional services provided under this Agreement will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards, and that Corio's remedy for breach of this warranty shall be re-performance of the non-conforming services or, if Commerce One is unable to re-perform them within thirty (30) days, a refund of the fees paid for such services.
